title: Map regulated workloads to current compliance requirements
description: Map controls to the current regulatory standard, such as PCI DSS 4.x, and validate the AKS shared-responsibility model. Use supported FIPS-enabled images where mandated; an architecture example or Azure certification does not itself make an application compliant.

documentation.title: Map regulated workloads to current compliance requirements

title: Assess customer-managed encryption keys and their lifecycle
description: AKS encrypts data at rest using platform protection. If customer-managed keys are required, assess supported KMS options and Key Vault availability, permissions, purge protection, rotation, and recovery. The newer KMS data-encryption experience is documented as preview; do not treat it as a production default.

documentation.title: Assess customer-managed encryption keys and their lifecycle

detail: Distinguish legacy etcd KMS from the newer KMS data-encryption configuration. Check Kubernetes version, regional availability, and support status before enabling either; loss of a required key can make encrypted secrets unrecoverable.

title: Enforce risk-based image admission controls
description: Scan images in CI and continuously in the registry. Enforce approved registries, digest-based releases, and risk policy through supported admission controls. Verify the support status and actual enforcement of any vulnerability-aware integration, define time-bound exceptions with owners, and do not assume that registry scanning alone blocks deployment.

title: Integrate Key Vault using the Secrets Store CSI driver
description: Use the AKS Azure Key Vault provider with Microsoft Entra Workload ID. Enable rotation where required and test that applications reload mounted secrets. Environment variables do not automatically refresh; synchronizing to a Kubernetes Secret creates an additional stored copy.

documentation.title: Integrate Key Vault using the Secrets Store CSI driver

title: Monitor cloud security posture with Microsoft Defender for Cloud
description: Review Defender for Cloud recommendations and assign remediation owners. Connect security posture to Azure Policy and your incident workflow; distinguish posture assessment from the paid Defender for Containers runtime protection plan.

documentation.title: Monitor cloud security posture with Microsoft Defender for Cloud

title: Clean unused cached images without confusing cleanup with remediation
description: Evaluate AKS Image Cleaner for unused images on nodes. It does not patch images or remove vulnerable containers that are currently running: rebuild the image and redeploy affected workloads to remediate those risks.

documentation.title: Clean unused cached images without confusing cleanup with remediation

title: Enable Microsoft Defender for Containers
description: Microsoft Defender for Containers provides protections for your Kubernetes clusters wherever they're running (AKS and on-premises)

documentation.title: Introduction to Microsoft Defender for Containers

title: Use Azure Policy for Kubernetes to ensure cluster compliance
description: Azure Policy integrates with the Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) to apply at-scale enforcements and safeguards on your clusters in a centralized, consistent manner.

documentation.title: Azure Kubernetes Services Governance with Azure Policy

score.graph: where type=='microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' | extend compliant = (isnotnull(properties.addonProfiles.azurepolicy) and properties.addonProfiles.azurepolicy.enabled==true) | distinct id,compliant

title: Separate system and application node pools
description: In AKS Standard, dedicate appropriately sized Linux system pools to critical cluster components and run applications on user pools. Use the CriticalAddonsOnly taint where appropriate and provide production redundancy. System pools are not the managed control plane.

documentation.title: Separate system and application node pools

title: Migrate legacy service principals and rotate remaining credentials
description: Migrate cluster infrastructure to managed identities. Where a legacy service principal remains, rotate credentials before expiry under an audited policy and test the change; a fixed quarterly interval alone does not manage credential risk.

documentation.title: Migrate legacy service principals and rotate remaining credentials

title: Use a private registry for your images, such as ACR
description: Azure Container Registry allows you to build, store, and manage container images and artifacts in a private registry

title: Continuously assess cluster security configuration
description: Run supported CIS-aligned configuration assessments and review drift in RBAC, network exposure, admission policy, and workload permissions. Record accepted risks and remediation dates rather than treating an assessment score as proof of compliance.

title: Evaluate confidential computing for specific threat models
description: Evaluate the supported AKS confidential-computing options against your workload and compliance needs. Distinguish application enclaves from confidential virtual machines and confidential containers; verify SKU, region, attestation, OS, and feature support rather than assuming every container automatically runs inside an enclave.

title: Define app separation requirements (namespace/nodepool/cluster)
description: Plan for multi-tenant clusters and separation of resources and use logical or physical isolation in your AKS clusters

documentation.title: Best practices for cluster isolation in AKS

title: Evaluate Dedicated Hosts only for explicit isolation requirements
description: Use Azure Dedicated Hosts when dedicated physical capacity is required and supported for the node configuration. Plan host capacity, failure domains, maintenance, and additional cost; this does not remove application-level security responsibilities.

documentation.title: Evaluate Dedicated Hosts only for explicit isolation requirements

title: Enforce Pod Security Standards and least-privilege containers
description: Apply Pod Security Admission or equivalent Azure Policy controls. Progress from audit to enforcement; for Linux workloads prefer restricted settings, non-root users, seccomp RuntimeDefault, dropped capabilities, read-only filesystems, and no privilege escalation. Document narrowly scoped exceptions.

documentation.title: Enforce Pod Security Standards and least-privilege containers

title: Protect node metadata and minimize node identity permissions
description: Minimize node managed-identity permissions and use federated workload identities. AKS IMDS restriction is documented as preview, applies to non-host-network pods, and requires assessment of support terms and compatibility. Do not assume a generic NetworkPolicy blocks all metadata or host-network access.

documentation.title: Protect node metadata and minimize node identity permissions
